activities.name: Basic jump-rope hop
activities.description: Basic jump-rope hop is a conditioning activity with a distinct movement or apparatus. Pace, distance and duration are choices for a separate personal plan, not a target implied by the catalog.
setup: Use a rope of suitable length with clear space and non-slip footing.
execution: Turn the rope from the wrists and use small two-foot hops with soft landings.
Reduce pace or stop while movement and breathing remain controlled.
cues: Use a pace appropriate to your current experience and conditions.
commonMistakes: Starting at a pace that prevents a controlled finish.
Treating a library entry as a fitness or medical clearance.

benefits.text: Provides repeated movement that can be used for conditioning practice.
benefits.qualification: Conditioning opportunity, not a guaranteed cardiovascular, weight-loss or therapeutic outcome. Effect depends on intensity, dose and personal suitability.

precautions: Stop for pain, pinching, numbness, dizziness or loss of control. This is general activity information, not an injury assessment or treatment.
If injured, recently operated on, or working under clinical restrictions, follow your qualified clinician rather than this catalog.
Stop for chest pain, faintness or unusual breathlessness; seek appropriate medical help. Heat, traffic, water and moving machinery need separate safety judgment.
modifications: Practice without a rope or use a slower turn.

activities.name: Ankle CARs
activities.description: Ankle CARs explores comfortable available ankle movement with deliberate control. It is not a rehabilitation prescription or evidence of affiliation with FRC or Kinstretch.
setup: Sit and support the lower leg so the foot can move freely.
Begin unloaded or with minimal body-weight pressure; stabilize the supports before moving.
execution: Point the foot, turn through a gentle inward arc, draw it toward the shin and travel through an outward arc; reverse slowly.
Stop before compensation or discomfort, return to the starting position and choose the other side when relevant.
cues: Keep the knee quiet and avoid gripping the toes to enlarge the circle.
Smaller controlled range is preferable to forcing an end position.
commonMistakes: Using momentum or outside force to gain range.
Keep the knee quiet and avoid gripping the toes to enlarge the circle.

benefits.text: Offers deliberate practice of the specified joint motion and awareness of compensations.
benefits.qualification: Describes practice intent, not proven pain treatment, cartilage change, joint-health improvement or injury prevention.

precautions: Stop for pain, pinching, numbness, dizziness or loss of control. This is general activity information, not an injury assessment or treatment.
If injured, recently operated on, or working under clinical restrictions, follow your qualified clinician rather than this catalog.
Do not push through pain or pinching, use maximal tension, or let another person force the joint. If symptoms persist, stop and seek qualified assessment.
modifications: Use a smaller pain-free arc and additional stable support.
Omit loaded end positions and separate the directions of motion if a circle is not comfortable.

If injured, recently operated on, or working under clinical restrictions, follow your qualified clinician rather than this catalog.
Tradition and sequence context do not establish individual suitability or any medical benefit.
Do not use the hands or a partner to force knee rotation or lotus/leg-behind-head range. Stop for knee or ankle pressure.
modifications: Use teacher-selected supports or a simpler separately chosen posture; a modification is not an automatic series advancement.
Keep the legs unbound in a comfortable seated position; omit lotus or leg-behind-head placement when not established.
